page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of memory per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between raw compute and memory-bound operations. The server exhibits poor single-core and weak multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests. However, it achieves average performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, with a notable top-tier rating in text processing. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read/write operations fall within the average range, though the PassMark memory score is classified as weak. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all perform at average levels.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server type offers a qualitative cost-efficiency profile suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments. This configuration is appropriate for large-scale caching, in-memory databases, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose web serving where memory capacity is the primary constraint.
